 Job Job is the first game to be announced for The Jackbox Party Pack 8 , having been announced on April 29, 2021.

 Players who have entered the game become each other's colleagues who have applied for this employment opportunity. But there is only one job. Therefore, M. Bubbles , the manager, has developed a revolutionary new hiring process in which they will interrogate everyone at once and force them to judge each other.

 Gameplay [ ] 

 In the first round, called "icebreaker", you will be asked questions, your job is to answer these as simply as possible with at least 5 words present.

 After the "icebreaker" round comes the "interview" round, where difficult interview questions are asked. But instead of typing their answers, players should use the words of fellow interviewers to answer questions. On your device, click on any word to add it to your answer. 

 If you regret what you picked, click on the word again to delete it.

 If you don't like where you placed it, you can also hold down the words to rearrange them.

 Feeling stuck? Then you can click on "shuffle" or "sort" to get new inspiration, or "start for me" to let the game pick out free random words to get you started.

This repeats for the second round, however this time players need to answer two hypothetical questions about office life. In the final round, you need to write a last personal statement about yourself, for example:

 I am <simply present. to job>
My goal <is to hold regret round office>

 Audience Integration [ ] 

 Audience members are the "board of directors" and will vote for answers during the interviews. During the writing process, they will be able to make motivational posters that will show up in the background.

 Trivia [ ] 

 Every character icon references a key aspect of Jackbox Games' library. Every icon also has a unique voting SFX based off of the game they reference.
 One is a heart, referencing Monster Seeking Monster .

 One is a duck, quite morbidly referencing Joke Boat .

 One is a reference to the Drawful 's mascot: Sexy owl.

 One is a shirt, referencing Tee K.O. .

 One is a dodecahedron, referencing DODE , the host of Push the Button .

 One is pile of poop, referencing Civic Doodles .

 One is a pixelated bomb, referencing Bomb Corp. .

 One is a skull, referencing Trivia Murder Party .

 One is the silhouette of the faker from Fakin' It .

 One is Jackbox Games' mascot: Jackhead.

 One is a robot, referencing Mad Verse City .

 One is Mayonnaise 's silhouette, the host of Split the Room .

 One is a screw, referencing You Don't Know Jack .

 One is a moon/banana, referencing one of Quiplash 3 's avatars.
 This is the first game in the franchise to feature every player being a direct reference to another game in the series.

 In one of the possible animations when writing icebreakers, M. Bubbles finds a sentient stapler inside a serving of jelly, a likely reference to The Office , where Jim pranks Dwight by doing the same thing, only with a regular, non-sentient stapler.

 The fonts used are ClickClackv4, ClickClackHighlightv10, Bourton Handv2, Bourton Phatv2, Foundation Sans Roman, KG Corner of the Sky, WinthorpeScSb-Regular & Museo 700 Italic.

 Before settling on the suitcase with eyes, Jackbox Games had considered may other potential logos for the game, including newspaper clippings, folders, and even some with hands and markers! [↑]

 Job Job is a party video game and one of five games featured in The Jackbox Party Pack 8 .

 Gameplay

 Every player is prompted to first write verbose answers to icebreaker questions on their device, with a 5-word minimum. There will be three icebreakers to be answered in the first round , later rounds will have different prompts and one less icebreaker apiece.

 During the writing phases, the audience can also make custom motivational pictures by picking an image and filling in a blank with a pre-written sentence. These pictures will then appear in the game.

 Once all icebreakers have been submitted, two separate prompts will show up on the device's screen along with three other players' icebreaker answers, with all words and symbols (like dots, commas, etc.) dissected from the original text. The player can then use these words (along with words from the actual question itself) to 'construct' a response to the prompts given to them.

 After all players submit their responses to their respective prompts, the game will show one of the prompts along with two submitted answers to them (in a " Quiplash "-styled fashion ) of which the other players and audience members will vote for their favorite.

 When everyone's votes are in, the winner of the round will earn the bigger percentage of the points depending on how many people voted for their answer; the players who got their words featured on the winning answer will get 50 points per word used. If the player who arranged the winning answer managed to use words from all three of the players' answers, they'll also be able to receive a 50-point "Rainbow Bonus". If they manage to sweep all the votes, M. Bubbles' arms will turn golden and water will spray out of them, with the text Synergy at the bottom, and they get all the points.

 The second round works pretty much the same as the first, but with more office-related prompts.

 The third and final round consists of two separate personal statements (like "I LOVE [blank]" and "I HATE [blank]," for example) of which the player has to complete the sentences with the words on their device.

 Once all three rounds have concluded, the final scoreboard is shown, with the player with the most votes officially joining the team, as well as M. Bubbles firing someone (e.g. Allard) right after.

 During the game's credits, the full answers who've been used the most throughout all the answers in the game will be shown at the bottom left side of the screen, along with the amount of times their words have been used.

 In the game's overview, one can buy shirts containing players' answers in the game.

 Development

 The design team for the game are as follows:

 Brooke Breit - Director and Original Concept

 Ryan DiGiorgi - Lead Editorial

 Michael Siciliano - Lead Gameplay Engineer

 Owen Watson - Lead Artist

 Brian Chard - Audio Lead

 Lena Guerrero - Lead Jackbox.TV Engineer

 Allison Flom - QA Lead

 Trivia

 Whilst players are typing and answering their prompts, some animations will happen in the background:
 Most of these will include M. Bubbles doing some weird activities: like kitting yarn, vomiting into a flower pot, among others. But some other animations will contain other animate inanimate objects: like the table eating a computer mouse, part of the wallpaper ripping to show a disembodied beating heart on the inside, among others.

 Other animations also include returning characters from other Jackbox titles, like a robot from Mad Verse City and Chuck Hull from Joke Boat , to name a few.

 During the icebreaker portion of the second round, M. Bubbles will always answer a miscellaneous phone call from an employee.

 If you manage to win with an answer using all of the words from only one player, M. Bubbles will personally call you out for being unoriginal.

 If a player doesn't submit anything for their answer, it'll be replaced with one that explicitly shows the player didn't submit an answer.

 This game uses the following fonts:
 Click Clack , designed by Ethan Dunham for Fonthead. [ 1 ] 

 Bourton Base , designed by Kimmy Kirkwood for Kimmy Design. [ 2 ]
